cues.say: Component 18: Timeouts, retries, circuit breaker. Three rules for any outside call: give up after N seconds, retry with growing waits, and stop calling for a while after repeated failures. You'll bring this up during version one, wherever you call an outside service.
Think of it as: Hang up on hold music, call back later, and stop dialing if the line is clearly dead. Use it for stripe, SMS, and any outside service.
Here's a real scenario. Game day: Stripe calls slow down from 300 milliseconds to 8 seconds.
Without it: Each checkout ties up a server for 8 seconds.
Every server waits on Stripe; even the menu stops loading.
With it: 2 seconds timeout: fail fast, retry once with the same key.
5 failures in a row: the circuit opens for 30 seconds.
Checkout says try again in a minute; the rest stays fast.
Why it works: One slow outside service shouldn't take down everything else.
In the interview, say: Retries are safe only because the call carries an idempotency key.
A few related terms you may hear.
Backoff: Wait longer each retry: 100, 200, 400 milliseconds.
Jitter: Random extra wait, so clients don't retry in sync.
Circuit breaker: Closed, then open (fail fast), then half-open (test one call).
Bulkhead: Separate connection pools per service, like a ship's compartments.
